description.narrative:
Interpeace har ansökt om 77 miljoner SEK i stöd för att genomföra insatsen '’Reinforcing community capacity for social cohesion and reconciliation through Societal Trauma Healing in Rwanda’, 2021-2025, mellan juli 2021 till juni 2022. Insatsen genomförs i samarbete med Prison Fellowship Rwanda (RFP), Haguruka och Dignity in Detention Organisation (DiDe).
Insatsens mål syftar till att stärka den mentala hälsan hos de som drabbats av folkmordet mot Tutsierna 1994 och deras emotionella och finansiella resiliens och i längde verka för hållbar fred. Mer specifikt syftar insatsen på att stärka återintegreringen av fängelsfångar dömda för folkmordsbrott som kommer att släppas under de kommande fyra åren och minska risker relaterad till återintegreringen, såsom förväntade ökade fall av könsbaserat våld, spänningar, konflikter och ökade nivåer av trauma. Insatsen arbetar även mer Rwandas yngre befolkning för att minska intergenerationstrauma och därmed motverka radikalisering och ökade spänningar bland den yngre generationen. Programmet är uppdelat i fyra resultatområden med specifika mål och aktiviteter, (1) Förbättrad läkning och psykosocial motståndskraft bland män, kvinnor och unga i samhället och inom fängelser, (2) Förbättrad social sammanhållning och återintegrering av folkmordsdömda fängelsegångar (3) Inkluderande och kollektiva försörjningsmöjligheter för män, kvinnor och unga i samhället och fängelser för att förbättra välbefinnandet, social samanhållning och försoning, och (4) Stärkande av nationell policy och program inom ramen för helande, social sammanhållning och försoning, samt försörjningsmöjligheter för de fattigaste, inklusive släppta fängelsefångar och de som överlevde folkmordet mot Tutsierna.
Sverige står som enskild finansiär av insatsen men förhoppningen är antalet givare kommer att öka under insatsens gång vid en eventuell utökning av insatser till andra distrikt. CKCK MSK kommer vidareförmedlas till partnerorganisationer samt TVET-institutioner.

Interpeace has submitted to the Embassy a proposal for a four-year programme titled, ’Reinforcing community capacity for social cohesion and reconciliation through Societal Trauma Healing in Rwanda’. The proposed duration of the programme is July 2021 to June 2025, and the budget is 77 million SEK. The contribution will be implemented in close collaboration with Prison Fellowship Rwanda ( RFP), HAGURUKA and Dignity in Detention Organization (DiDe).
The proposed programme aims to address and heal the psycho-social wounds that has been caused by the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi and strengthen social cohesion, trust building and socio-economic development with the longer perspective of promoting sustainable peace in Rwanda. This will be achieved through trauma healing, community dialogue, and small-scale livelihood projects. A strong emphasis is put on the releases of prisoners convicted of crimes relating to the Genocide against the Tutsi and their reintegration back into their communities as well as on youth, and their ability to heal from inter-generational trauma. The program is divided into four result areas with specific goals and activities, (1) Improved healing and psychosocial resilience among men, women and young people in society and in prisons, (2) Improved social cohesion and reintegration of genocidal convictions (3) Inclusion and collective livelihoods for men, women and young people in society and prisons for the development of well-being, social cohesion and reconciliation; genocide survivor.
Sweden is the sole financier of the contribution, but there is an anticipation that additional donors will fund a potential up-scale of the programme. CKCK MSK will be passed on to partner organizations and TVET institutions.

The objective of the programme is to strengthen psychosocial and socioeconomic resilience for sustainable peace among communities in five districts in Rwanda through five outcomes:
Enhanced healing and psychosocial resilience among men, women, youth and other vulnerable groups in communities and prisons.
Enhanced social cohesion and prisoners psychosocial reintegration.
Improved socio-economic inclusion and collective livelihood opportunities for men, women, youth, and other vulnerable groups.
National policies and programmes on healing, social cohesion and collective livelihoods are informed by lessons learned from programme interventions.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
In the past period, the Programme has continued implementation in 5 districts.
Work is based on the roll out of four "protocols" for different types of group therapy for people affected by the Genocide against the Tutsi. These include (1)the socio-therapy protocols to advance social cohesion, (2) resilience oriented therapy to strengthen mental health services, the (3) multifamily therapy, and the (4) collaborative livelihoods protocol to promote sustainable livelihoods among groups that have undergone therapy. Also policy level work with government counterparts has moved forward significantly.
Key figures: 51 633 people reached in five districts, 25 sectors and 75 cells/villages (2 540 men 2 623 women) 153 healing spaces created, 2 115 participants (841 men 1 274 women) The baseline survey conducted in the five districts (2022) had demonstrated a high rate of mental health problems among the population, key factors affecting mental health being (by order of prevalence): Genocide related trauma, family conflicts, social tensions, and maladaptive family discussions about the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. In response, the program is demonstrating a measurable positive effect in strengthening healing and social cohesion (outcomes 1 & 3).
Through the group-based resilience oriented therapy protocols, the program strengthened the mental resilience of 211 participants (81 men 130 women) in 25 mixed groups (genocide survivors, genocide perpetrators, returnees and ex-combatants) created in the community. Facilitated by trained psychologists, participants were equipped with the necessary skills and tools for regulating emotions and behaviours. The comparison between the baseline and post intervention surveys shows that the prevalence of for example, depression dropped from 22.5% 8% and anxiety from 33.5% to 15.7%.
As part of the socio-therapy healing spaces, which facilitate a dialogue and mutual healing between genocide survivors, perpetrators, returnees and ex-combatants a total of 1 758 community members (684 men 1 074 women) completed healing sessions in 119 healing spaces. The pre and postscreening results show that the mixed healing spaces enhanced individual healing, trust and tolerance, specifically, between genocide survivors and perpetrators and their offspring. The post intervention evaluation showed an increase in mutual trust up to the highest possible score, as well as a significant increase in forgiveness practices and willingness to participate in collective activities.
Based on the trust created during the healing process, and with support from the program, applying the livelihoods protocols ("CoLive protocol"), all graduating healing groups have decided to transform to collaborative livelihoods groups, such as savings and credit groups or other income generating activities, which provides incentives for them to work together and strengthen the bonds formed during the healing spaces.Participant testimonials show that these activities have also helped participants to challenge traditional gender roles in business management and enhanced women´s leadership roles and confidence.
The program has also successfully continued generating evidence and knowledge to inform policies and programming (Outcome 4).
According to Interpeace, there is a high degree of buy-in from government counterparts. As for the implementation of the protocols, currently Resilience oriented therapy is being implemented in 32 public mental health care structures (20 health centres, 7 district hospitals, and 5 prisons), in addition to 27 community-based spaces) created by the program. The focus will increasingly be to support the institutionalization of the approaches and protocols in and beyond the districts covered by the program.
Interpeace's partnership with the Ministry of National Unity and Civic Engagement (MINUBUMWE) has deepened. Interpeace has supported the ministry to develop the new concept of Community Resilience, in line with the Ministry's policy shifts from a reconciliation focus to a broader approach of resilience to conflict. Interpeace and MINUBUMWE developed a framework with resilience indicators that can be used to structure future research activities, policies, and programs.
The program supported MINUBUMWE in reviewing the national civic and peace education curriculum and to adapt it to the lessons and socio-emotional skills needs identified by the program. Work is starting to as well as a new Unity and Reconciliation Barometer.
Another example knowledge generation is a study on inter generational legacies, their transmission, and effects on engagement in risky behaviors among post-genocide youth in Rwanda, which was conducted in partnership with a local youth led organisation, Rwanda We Want.
As an example of stakeholder engagement, Interpeace in in partnership with Never Again Rwanda and the Aegis Trust, organised Rwanda Youth Talks, an event that created a platform for youth, policy makers, civil-society organisations and government officials to discuss the nexus between peace-building and environmental protection and the role of young people.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
